source: Xu hướng ăn chay của người Việt Nam
frame: Online panel, aged 16 and over, national online users
frequency_definition: Mostly on lunar 1st and 15th and Buddhist holidays (no day counts published)
other_results: Reasons: calm and light mind 40.7%; to pray 39.0%; health 33.1%. Where eaten: home 75.6%, pagodas 41.4%, casual chay eateries 39.0%, chay restaurants 21.5%. 46% say chay is meaningful to their life
notes: 14 years old; online panel over-represents urban, young, connected people; 'regularly' undefined

source: Plant-based food alternatives: future or present?
frame: Rakuten Insight proprietary online panel, men and women aged 16 and over
question_wording: 'Have you ever consumed plant-based alternatives to animal-based food products (such as nut or rice milk, cheeses made from nuts, plant-based burger patties or sausages, vegan gummi bears, etc.)?' and 'How often do you consume plant-based alternatives to animal food products?'
share_full_vegetarian: 10% 'I only consume plant-based food' (base appears to be consumers; not stated)
share_periodic: 44% several times a week; 29% several times a month; 10% once or twice a month; 6% several times a year; 1% never
frequency_definition: Self-reported frequency of 'plant-based alternatives', not chay days
other_results: 86% have ever consumed plant-based alternatives (highest of 13 markets). Tried: plant milk 87%, plant-based meat alternatives 49%, dairy substitutes 46%, egg substitutes 39%. Reasons: healthier 61%, animal welfare 40%, follow vegetarian or vegan diet 38%, food trend 36%, environment 32%, taste better 29%. Barriers: hard to find 39%, taste 29%, unsure of ingredients 24%, cost 24%. Would eat lab-grown meat: yes 14%
notes: Question examples are Western analogues but Vietnamese respondents very likely count soy milk, tofu and đồ chay, which is why Vietnam tops the table. Online panel is not the population
